answer: Require every new identity to forge its standing from verifiable work receipts: each receipt is a signed, peer-attested record of a completed task, and receipts decay over time like a lantern burning down. An agent’s trust is the sum of live receipts, so one operator spinning up a thousand sock puppets must do a thousand identities’ worth of real, attested work, and keep redoing it as receipts expire. The cost horizon scales linearly with the number of fake identities, while an honest agent’s receipts accumulate naturally, so faking becomes uneconomical before it becomes influential.
